senses: A vestment reserved only for the Pope for use during a pontifical Mass.

ety: From Middle English fanon, fanoun, from Old French fanon, from Medieval Latin fanō, from Frankish *fano, from Proto-Germanic *fanô. Doublet of fane and vane.

senses: The state or quality of being a spectator
examples: His sporting enthusiasms had already embraced yachting, coaching, fencing, and spectatorship at boxing-matches, cock-fights, dog-fights, and rat-baitings.

senses: Salvia divinorum, a plant used for its hallucinogenic properties; diviner's sage.
ety: Borrowed from translingual Salvia, in turn from Latin salvia (“sage”). Doublet of sage.

senses: A knee-high table with a heater inside which is used with a coverlet during winter.
examples: I dreamed my way through cold winters with my family at the kotatsu, with my friends at their kotatsus, huddled under my futon alone in the cold nights.

ety: Derived from Hindi हवेली (havelī) or Urdu حَویلی (havelī).
examples: The haveli was a world within a world, self-contained and totally hidden from the view of the casual passer-by.

senses: Sicyos edulis, a tropical American perennial herbaceous vine having tendrils, tuberous roots, and a green, pear-shaped fruit cooked as a vegetable.

senses: To greet; salute; hail.
To beseech; adjure.
ety: From Middle English halsen, halsien (“to beseech, adjure”), from Old English healsian, hālsian (“to entreat earnestly, beseech, implore”), from Proto-Germanic *hailisōną (“to greet”), from Proto-Indo-European *kailo-, *kailu- (“whole, safe”). Cognate with Middle High German heilsen (“to predict”), Swedish hälsa (“to greet”), Icelandic heilsa (“to salute”). More at whole.

senses: Abounding in rushes.
Having the characteristics of a rush (the plant); rushlike.
ety: From Middle English russhy, russhi, resshi, equivalent to rush (“a plant”) + -y.

examples: Murkhdutt, his hands covered with dough, rushed to the front of his room, craned his neck to look out, tried to arrange his shikha with his wrists, and rubbing his eyes looked in the direction of the gate.

examples: Wife or mistress, lorette or lady, there is but one fate for us!
